newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone falls on sales disappointment.
newsitem.headline: Danone falls on sales disappointment.

text.p: Shares in food group Danone fell on Friday on disappointment with the group's nine-month like-for-like sales rise of two percent, brokers said.

"The group suffered from a decreasing activity in Germany and Belgium and flat activity in France and Spain," a brokerage said in its morning comment. "International growth is entirely due to dairy products activities in central Europe when sales went up 50 percent...Favourable mix/price seen in H1 is confirmed."
Shares in Danone were down 2.13 percent at 735 francs at 0940 GMT while the bourse's CAC-40 index was up 0.7 percent.
Nine-month sales were 63.23 billion francs, compared with 60.21 billion.

It said its third-quarter business was hit by poor weather which cut into beer and mineral water sales. Currency conversion differences, due mainly to the lira's rise and changes in sales structure, added 151 million francs to sales.
First-time integration of dairy product operations in eastern Europe, China and Argentina, biscuits in Greece and China, and beer in China added 1,628 million francs.
